protocol: Walk-forward over 20 test days, 2026-09-28 to 2026-10-17 (all 9 exam days, and the 2026-10-02 holiday, fall inside). For every stream (electricity, water), horizon (6 h, 12 h) and test day d, the model is retrained at midnight d on features(hourly(as_of=d)), using only target hours before d and only meter rows already received by d, then used to forecast the 24 target hours of day d. Test rows have an observed target; features look back from the forecast origin (target hour minus horizon), plus the same hour yesterday and last week, and the temperature is the real daily mean of the target date, a stand-in for a weather forecast. Methods: 'simple guess' predicts the same hour yesterday; 'our model' is forecast.fit (gradient boosting, up to 300 iterations) retrained every day; 'our model, no retraining' is one fit at midnight 2026-09-28 used for all 20 days (the drift comparison, it has never seen an exam day); 'small model' is the same daily retraining with up to 100 iterations, 15 leaves per tree and learning rate 0.1. All methods are scored on the same rows, dropping any row where a prediction is missing. Errors are split by the target date's day type (exam vs everything else, so the holiday and weekends count as normal): MAE in kWh or litres, and percent error = 100 * sum|error| / sum(actual). A spike is an actual value above the 95th percentile of that stream, building and hour of day over all data before 2026-09-28 (a fixed threshold); a spike is caught when the prediction is above the same threshold, and a false alarm is a prediction above it when the actual was not. size_kb is the joblib (compress=3) file size, train_s the mean seconds per fit (the single fit for no retraining), time_ms the median wall time of one building's 12-hour forecast (12 rows) on one core; for the simple guess it times reading the stored same-hour-yesterday values. Everything is measured on single-threaded scikit-learn 1.4.1.
